title: The ox-herding pictures
hook: Kakuan sets the Zen path out as ten pictures of a herder and his ox, and the last one walks back into town
tomorrow: what has the herder lost, and why doesn't he know it?

segments.voice: This week was about passing it on. One breath for a child, on steady ground. Listen first. Name the home. An invitation, the choice left free. Jacob's roadside: this is it. And yesterday, Yudhishthira and the dog on the last ridge. Now the summit gets a map.
screen: `ONE BREATH · LISTEN FIRST · NAME THE HOME` → `AN INVITATION · THIS IS IT · THE LAST RIDGE`

segments.voice: A storyboard, a comic strip, the little drawings on a flat-pack instruction sheet: some things are easiest to follow in pictures. A Chinese Zen teacher named Kuoan, known in Japan as Kakuan, set out the whole spiritual path as ten pictures, each with a short poem. In the first, a herder stands in wild, tall grass, searching. He has lost his ox. Why an ox? Zen teachers read the ox as your own true nature: the very thing you're looking for when you start looking.
screen: `A STORYBOARD FOR THE PATH.` → `KAKUAN'S TEN PICTURES.` → `A HERDER HAS LOST HIS OX.`

segments.voice: Then the pictures move. He finds the tracks. He glimpses the ox. He catches it, and it fights him. He tames it. He rides it home, playing a flute. Then the ox is forgotten, and the herder sits alone. Then an empty circle: ox and herder both forgotten. Then the source: a river, a tree, simply as they are. And the tenth picture is the surprise. The herder walks back into the marketplace, among ordinary people, with open, helping hands. That is the Zen teaching the series carries: the search doesn't end alone on a mountain. It ends back in town, helping. Look at the week you just walked and you can see the tenth picture in it. A child's first breath. A friend heard out. A teaching handed on with its home. Starting tomorrow, the summit walks the ten pictures one at a time, beginning in the tall grass.
screen: `TRACKS, A GLIMPSE, THE CATCH.` · `RIDING HOME, PLAYING A FLUTE.` · `THE EMPTY CIRCLE.` · `BACK TO THE MARKETPLACE.` · then, large: `TEN PICTURES.`

segments.voice: Let the ten pictures pass through your mind like a slow slideshow: searching, tracks, a glimpse, the catch, the taming, riding home, the ox forgotten, the empty circle, the source, the marketplace. Notice which one feels most like where you are right now. Then rest in that picture until the bell.
The ox-herding pictures: Kakuan's ten Zen pictures of a herder seeking his ox, ending back in town with helping hands.
Pocket this: ten pictures, and the last one walks back into town. See you in the tall grass.
